inputs.share_count_basis: Issued 72,088,327 less treasury 976,836 at 2026-09-30 (H1 FY2027 tanshin, Notes (4)). No dilutive securities: diluted EPS reported as '-'. Held flat; the H1 FY2027 buyback (JPY 3,503m) is value-neutral in this model and already in the count.
inputs.net_debt_note: 2026-09-30 balance sheet. Debt = short-term borrowings 13,986 + commercial paper 13,000 + current LTB 4,414 + current bonds 10,000 + bonds 25,000 + long-term borrowings 91,473 = 157,873 (excludes lease liabilities 7,669, which are deducted separately in equity_bridge; the company's own 'interest-bearing debt' of 165,544 includes them). Cash = cash and deposits 47,465.
inputs.sbc_source: Not separately disclosed (J-GAAP filer). Only a directors' performance-linked share-award provision of JPY 82-98m exists; immaterial against JPY 349bn revenue, so SBC is carried as an explicit 0% line. SBC-zero market: house and street bases coincide.
inputs.interest_income_note: Interest income JPY 360m FY2026 is NOT stripped from last_fcf because the company is a net debtor (net debt JPY 110bn, ~5x the FCF base). Note that the forward flows are built from operating profit, so interest and dividend income and equity-method profit (all below operating profit) are outside the flows by construction; their source assets (investment securities) are added in equity_bridge per the matching-asset rule.
inputs.buyback_note: JPY 3,503m treasury purchase in H1 FY2027 (first material buyback since the JPY 21.65bn of FY2018). FY2026 was JPY 4m. Value-neutral here; recorded so the reader can see the flat count is being partly funded.
inputs.fy_label_note: CSV/DCF FY labels are the year in which the fiscal year ENDS: FY2026 = year ended 31 March 2026, which the company calls 'Fiscal 2025'. The company's FBP 2030 target year (its 'FY2030') is FY2031 here, i.e. forecast year 5.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-30T06:30:00Z (TSE regular close 15:30 JST; Yahoo Finance chart API)
inputs.last_fcf_basis: FY2026 (year ended 2026-03-31): OCF 50,985 less capex 29,111 = 21,874. Owner FCF = reported FCF since SBC is zero and interest income is not stripped (net debtor). Mid-cycle reference: FY2014-FY2026 owner-FCF median JPY 19.5bn, mean JPY 12.9bn (dragged by the FY2023 energy-cost / working-capital trough of -43.7bn), FY2024-26 average JPY 25.3bn. FY2026 is therefore close to mid-cycle, not a peak; the forward build normalises on margins rather than on this single year.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in JPY. Risk-free 10y JGB ~1.7% (Oct 2026), ERP 6.0%, beta ~1.2 for a cyclical chemicals/cement/semiconductor-materials conglomerate gives cost of equity ~8.9%. Debt is ~37% of capital at market (JPY 165bn interest-bearing debt vs ~JPY 280bn market cap) at ~1.2% pre-tax (R&I 'A' rating), ~0.9% after tax. Pure market-weight WACC is ~5.9%; the company's own disclosed WACC is 6.5%. House default for JPY industrials is ~9%, but that is an all-equity keiretsu-supplier figure. Used 7.0% across all three scenarios: above the mechanical 5.9% to reflect BoJ normalisation (rising JGB yields), FBP 2030's intent to de-lever toward a lower D/E, and the thin JGB base; below the 9% house figure because the balance sheet genuinely carries low-cost debt. Cyclicality is charged in the scenario flows and weights, not in the rate (risk charged once; same WACC in bear/base/bull).
inputs.lease_treatment: (A) Leases as debt. J-GAAP filer: operating leases are expensed inside operating profit already; finance-lease liabilities (JPY 1,725m current + 5,944m non-current = 7,669m at 2026-09-30) are deducted once in equity_bridge and NOT deducted from the flows (lease principal sits in financing 'Other, net'). Capex path covers leased-asset renewal.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests JPY 19,233m (2026-09-30 book, up from 14,725m after a subsidiary share issuance to third parties in H1 FY2027) deducted once in equity_bridge. Flows are consolidated. NCI's profit share is small (loss attributable to NCI JPY -84m H1 FY2027), so deducting the full book is the conservative side.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing: operating company, non-US, cyclical -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md). Not a bank/REIT/LIC. Tokuyama is a diversified chemicals group: Chemicals (caustic soda, VCM/PVC, soda ash; ~30% of sales), Cement (~19%), Electronic & Advanced Materials (semiconductor-grade polycrystalline silicon, IC chemicals, fumed silica, AlN thermal-management materials; ~26%), Life Science (dental materials, IVD/diagnostics incl. TLS Group consolidated from FY2026; ~14%), Eco Business and Others. Growth businesses (E&AM + Life Science + Eco) were 53% of operating profit in FY2026 vs 30% in FY2021. Cycle drivers: caustic/VCM spreads and naphtha/energy costs (Chemicals OP ranged JPY 2.2bn to 16.8bn over FY2014-26), domestic cement demand (Cement OP -3.7bn to +9.5bn), and polysilicon/semiconductor demand (E&AM OP 3.3bn to 15.7bn). FY2027 guidance (revised 29 Oct 2026): net sales JPY 392.0bn (+12.2%, TLS consolidation plus price revisions), operating profit JPY 34.0bn (-8.2%; H1 was 13.6bn so H2 must deliver 20.4bn), net profit JPY 46.5bn which implies a ~JPY 25bn+ extraordinary gain (one-off gains on cross-shareholding sales per the Analysis JSON, possibly also the announced transfer of the domestic cement/solidification-agent sales business) -- that gain is a one-off and is NOT in the flows. Securities sold simply convert bridge assets to cash at roughly the carrying value already in equity_bridge, so the bridge is unchanged. FBP 2030 (its FY2030 = our FY2031) targets net sales 407.5bn, OP 57.0bn (14.0% margin), ROIC 9.1%, DOE 4.0%, EPS 551. The prior MTMP 2025 missed its OP target by 18% (37.0 vs 45.0) and revenue by 13%, so the plan is treated as the bull case, not the base. EBITDA here is operating profit plus ALL D&A (depreciation plus goodwill and customer-relationship amortisation, which started at ~JPY 3bn/yr with TLS), and da_pct includes the same amortisation, so EBIT ties to guided operating profit (year-1 EBIT ~JPY 34.1bn vs guidance 34.0bn). Price: regular TSE close, not after-hours.
inputs.segment_restructuring_note: Segments were re-cut in FY2022 (Specialty Products / Life & Amenity became Electronic & Advanced Materials / Life Science / Eco Business) and a revenue-recognition change cut reported Cement sales by ~JPY 44bn from FY2022; pre/post-FY2022 segment series are not comparable. Group-level margins are used for the historical ranges.

equity_bridge.item: Investment securities (listed strategic holdings, equity-method affiliates, unlisted at cost) less deferred tax on unrealised gain
equity_bridge.note: JPY 61,982m book at 2026-09-30 less ~JPY 3.5bn tax on the JPY 11,623m AFS valuation difference. Matching-asset rule: dividend income, interest income and equity-method profit (~JPY 3bn/yr combined, all below operating profit) are outside the OP-based flows, so the assets enter the bridge. Company is actively divesting (11 -> 9 listed stocks in FY2026; JPY 2.1bn sold in H1 FY2027).

equity_bridge.item: Finance lease liabilities (treatment A: leases as debt)
equity_bridge.note: 1,725 current + 5,944 non-current at 2026-09-30; excluded from total_debt so deducted here exactly once.
2026-09-30 balance sheet; flows are consolidated so the NCI stock is deducted once here.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Blend of revenue 5yr CAGR (2.9%, FY2021-FY2026) and the FBP 2030 net sales CAGR target (3.1%). Equity CAGR (7.3%) is retained-earnings accumulation on a ~35% payout and overstates operating growth.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR 7.3-7.4% diverges >30% from revenue CAGR (-0.2% / 2.9%) and from EPS (33.3% 3yr off the FY2023 trough; -2.5% 5yr). Equity growth is retained earnings, not revenue growth; EPS CAGRs are cycle artefacts (FY2023 EPS 130 was the energy-cost trough, FY2021 EPS 351 a strong year). Growth rate taken from revenue and the plan, not from equity.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF (SBC zero, net debtor so interest income not stripped). FCF 3yr CAGR undefined: FY2023 owner FCF was -43,716 (OCF -11.8bn on a raw-material cost spike and working-capital build). Owner-FCF series FY2014-26 (JPY m): 4,198 / -1,698 / 15,764 / 3,319 / 46,359 / 21,766 / 32,658 / 19,514 / -5,901 / -43,716 / 24,237 / 29,770 / 21,874; median 19,514, FY2024-26 average 25,294. Operating margin FY2017-26 ranged 4.1% (FY2023) to 13.4% (FY2018), average 9.8%.

base.growth_note: Year 1 = FY2027 guidance JPY 392.0bn (+12.2%; TLS Group full-year consolidation in Life Science, chemicals/cement price revisions). Thereafter 1.5-2.0% nominal: Japan nominal GDP-like growth with E&AM/Life Science growth offset by structurally flat-to-declining domestic chemicals and cement. Year-5 revenue ~JPY 422bn, modestly above the FBP 2030 407.5bn target because guidance already reaches 392bn in year 1.
base.margin_note: Year 1 EBITDA 15.6% ties to guided OP 34.0bn plus ~27bn D&A (incl. ~3bn TLS amortisation). Mid-cycle 17.5% EBITDA = ~10.6% operating margin, the FY2017-26 average (9.8%) plus a modest mix uplift from growth businesses now 53% of OP. Well below the FBP 2030 14% OP-margin target, which is the bull case.
base.capex_note: FY2027 plan JPY 41.0bn accrual (10.5% of sales; polysilicon overseas bases, IVD). Glides to 7.5% by year 6 vs D&A 6.9%: modest net reinvestment consistent with 1-1.5% terminal growth. FY2022-26 capex/sales ranged 6.6-10.9%.
base.tax_note: Cash taxes paid have run 14-18% of operating profit for eight years (FY2026: 5,121 on OP 37,017) on DTAs (JPY 12.6bn), R&D credits and lower-taxed foreign subsidiaries. Ramped from 22% to the ~30% Japanese statutory rate by year 5 because the DTA shelter is finite.
base.wc_note: Manufacturer: receivables + inventories less payables ~JPY 115bn = 33% of revenue at FY2026. Growth consumes cash, so capture is -25% of incremental revenue (H1 FY2027 inventories alone rose JPY 12.8bn on the revenue step-up).
base.terminal_note: Terminal growth 1.0% (Japan nominal, commodity chemicals/cement declining domestically). Cap 14x terminal FCF, inside the method's 12-15x cyclical band; Gordon at 7%/1% would be 16.8x so the cap binds.

bull.narrative: FBP 2030 delivered: 21% EBITDA = ~14% operating margin by year 5 (the plan's 14.0% target), revenue ~JPY 460bn by year 5 on semiconductor-polysilicon and AlN demand plus IVD M&A; growth businesses pass 60% of OP.

bear.narrative: FY2027 H2 falls short of the implied JPY 20.4bn OP (year-1 EBITDA 14.0% = ~7% OP margin), then a polysilicon down-cycle, another naphtha/energy cost spike and shrinking domestic cement volumes hold the operating margin near 8%, below the 10-year average; revenue flat after the TLS step-up.

scenario_narratives.base: Mid-cycle normalisation. FY2027 lands on the revised guidance (sales JPY 392bn, OP JPY 34bn; H2 recovers on price pass-through and polysilicon volume after H1's 29% OP decline). The operating margin then rebuilds to ~10.6% (17.5% EBITDA) by year 4 -- the FY2017-26 average plus a small mix uplift as Electronic & Advanced Materials and Life Science (53% of OP) outgrow Chemicals and Cement -- but stops well short of the FBP 2030 14% target, which the company's track record (MTMP 2025 missed OP by 18%) does not support as a central case. Capex stays elevated at ~10% of sales through the overseas polysilicon and IVD build-out, then glides to 7.5%. Cash taxes ramp from the sheltered ~22% to the 30% statutory rate. Terminal FCF margin ~6.5%, in line with the FY2024-26 average of 7.3% less the higher tax rate. Axes: caustic/VCM spreads vs naphtha and energy costs; domestic cement volumes and price; semiconductor-grade polysilicon pricing and the AlN/thermal-management ramp on AI servers; the IVD/dental mix shift.
scenario_narratives.bull: FBP 2030 achieved. Semiconductor polysilicon and AlN thermal-management materials ride the AI-server and advanced-node cycle, the overseas high-purity polysilicon bases ramp on time, IVD (TLS Group, A&T) and dental compound at double digits, and Chemicals/Cement hold price discipline. Operating margin reaches the plan's 14.0% (21% EBITDA) by year 5 on ~JPY 460bn of revenue, ROIC passes the 9.1% target, and the 4% DOE policy plus buybacks lift returns. Terminal growth 1.5%, cap 15x. This case needs the cycle, execution and M&A to all go right, which is why it carries only 25% weight.
scenario_narratives.bear: Cycle turns against a plan built at the top. H2 FY2027 misses the implied JPY 20.4bn OP, polysilicon prices fall as Chinese capacity spills into semiconductor grades, naphtha and electricity costs spike again as in FY2023 (when OCF went negative), domestic cement shipments keep shrinking with Japan's construction labour shortage, and the TLS/A&T integration dilutes rather than lifts margin. Operating margin settles around 8% (15% EBITDA), below the 10-year average, with revenue flat after the TLS step-up. Capex cannot be cut quickly because the growth projects are committed. Terminal growth 0.5%, cap 12x.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bear raised to 25% because this is a commodity-exposed cyclical (Chemicals OP has swung 2bn-17bn, Cement -3.7bn to +9.5bn, E&AM 3bn-16bn within the last decade; FY2023 OCF was negative), net debt is ~JPY 110bn, and the FY2027 guide needs a strong H2 after a 29% H1 OP decline. Bull cut to 25% because it requires the FBP 2030 14% margin target, which has only been approached at the FY2017-18 cycle peak, and the prior plan missed its profit target by 18%. Balance sheet (equity ratio 49%, 'A' rating) rules out solvency risk, so the bear case is margin compression, not distress.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on a mid-cycle margin, not on any single year. Tokuyama is in the middle of a genuine portfolio shift from commodity chlor-alkali and cement toward semiconductor materials and diagnostics, and the market has priced the AI-polysilicon story in and partly out again (52-week range 3,533-5,768). The house base case gives the company the FY2017-26 average operating margin plus a modest mix uplift, charges the committed growth capex, lets the tax shelter expire, and caps the terminal multiple at 14x FCF. The bridge adds the JPY 62bn investment-securities portfolio (net of tax) because its income is outside the operating-profit-based flows, and deducts leases and NCI once each. The FY2027 net-profit guide of JPY 46.5bn contains a ~JPY 25bn extraordinary gain that is excluded from the flows and not bridged.
key_risks_to_valuation: Commodity cycle: caustic soda / VCM spreads and naphtha-electricity costs drive Chemicals OP across a JPY 2-17bn range; the base margin assumes mid-cycle, and a FY2023-style cost spike takes a year of FCF to zero or below.

Polysilicon pricing: semiconductor-grade polycrystalline silicon is the largest E&AM profit line; Chinese capacity creep into higher grades or a semiconductor downcycle would undercut the mix-uplift thesis.

Execution on FBP 2030 growth capex (~JPY 41bn in FY2027, overseas polysilicon bases, IVD M&A): the plan's returns are the bull case; stranded or late capex is the bear case. The prior plan missed its OP target by 18%.
Working capital: 33% of revenue is tied up in receivables and inventory, so every revenue step-up (TLS consolidation, price pass-through) consumes cash before it earns.

Cash tax normalisation: eight years at a 14-18% cash rate are assumed to end by year 5; if DTAs and credits persist the model is ~JPY 150-200/share too low, and if they expire faster it is modestly high.

Domestic cement: structural volume decline in Japanese construction; the announced transfer of the cement sales business may reshape reported revenue and margin in ways not yet visible in the filings read.
Bridge items: the JPY 58.5bn of investment securities is carried at book less tax; listed strategic holdings can fall with the market and unlisted/equity-method stakes are at cost.
